content.title: Technical Manager - Full Stack Developer
content.tagline: I bridge business and technical teams, and deliver enterprise systems end to end.
content.bio: Full-stack engineer with 12+ years of hands-on experience across frontend (Angular, React, TypeScript), backend (Node.js, Express, NestJS, Spring Boot), and embedded systems (C/C++), delivered across SaaS and fintech platforms for clients in Japan, the US, Singapore, and Bangladesh. Comfortable owning a feature end-to-end — architecture, API design, UI implementation, and deployment on AWS/Azure/GCP. Currently building Openfolio, a multi-tenant SaaS platform on NestJS, Next.js, and MongoDB.

items.title: Unified Logistics Platform
items.problem: Sales order processing, warehouse operations and delivery management ran as three disconnected processes, with conflicting workflows across departments.
items.solution: A unified platform integrating web and mobile applications with a centralized database, giving every department one view of the same order.
items.impact: Real-time visibility of orders, inventory and last-mile delivery, and manual coordination between teams largely removed.
items.role: Project Manager with end-to-end ownership of scope, roadmap and delivery.

bodies.business:
Sales order processing, warehouse operations and delivery management ran as three disconnected processes. Each department had built its own way of working, and every handoff between them was manual.

  • No real-time visibility of orders, inventory or last-mile delivery
  • Conflicting workflows across the sales, warehouse and delivery teams
  • Coordination between departments done by hand at every step
bodies.solution:
A unified logistics system integrating web and mobile applications with a centralized database, so every department works from one view of the same order.

  • Ran stakeholder alignment sessions across all three departments
  • Standardized the conflicting workflows into one agreed process
  • Designed a unified system architecture around that process

The outcome was improved collaboration between departments and higher adoption of the system itself.
bodies.role:
I owned this project end to end as Project Manager, from scope through rollout.

  • Owned project scope, roadmap and delivery
  • Gathered and prioritized requirements from the sales, warehouse and delivery teams
  • Defined the user journeys and workflows
  • Led Agile teams across development, QA, UI/UX and infrastructure
  • Coordinated system design decisions with the technical leads
  • Managed UAT, training and rollout

items.title: Digital Payment System for a Self-Service Platform
items.problem: A self-service SaaS platform had no way to take payment, so it could not turn its users into subscribers.
items.solution: A payment gateway module integrated into the platform, letting users subscribe and pay online.
items.impact: Approximately 20% increase in revenue, and the platform became a revenue-generating product.
items.role: Technical Project Manager and feature owner, from business requirements through delivery.

bodies.business:
A self-service SaaS platform had no way to take money. Users could sign themselves up but not subscribe, which capped the product short of being a business.

  • No online payment path, so no self-service revenue
  • Friction in the subscription process
  • Security and reliability both non-negotiable for anything handling payment
bodies.solution:
A payment gateway module integrated into the platform, turning it into a revenue-generating product with a seamless digital payment experience.

  • Translated business needs into clear technical specifications
  • Coordinated closely with the development team through delivery
  • Reduced friction in the subscription process

The result was a reliable, user-friendly payment flow and roughly 20% more revenue.
bodies.role:
I acted as Technical Project Manager and feature owner for the payment work.

  • Communicated with stakeholders to define the business requirements
  • Created the functional specification documents
  • Planned and managed the Agile sprints
  • Defined tasks for the development and QA teams
  • Led feature delivery
  • Ran training for the marketing team

items.title: Real-Time 3D Digital Twin for Real Estate
items.problem: Prospective buyers had to visit properties in person, and delivering a real-time 3D experience over the web normally demands high-end hardware.
items.solution: Digital twins of real estate buildings, explored through an interactive web experience built on pixel streaming.
items.impact: Remote property showcasing with no need for high-end user hardware, reducing physical visits and improving engagement.
items.role: Technical Project Manager, owning client communication, requirements and delivery.

bodies.business:
Showing a property meant getting people to it. Remote viewing existed, but a real-time 3D walkthrough of a building normally asks the viewer for hardware they do not have.

  • Physical visits required to evaluate a property
  • High-quality 3D environments too heavy for an ordinary machine
  • Delivering that experience over the web was the open technical question
bodies.solution:
A real-time 3D platform that builds digital twins of real estate buildings and lets people explore them from a browser, using pixel streaming so the rendering happens server-side.

  • Implemented a pixel streaming architecture
  • Coordinated system performance optimization across the team
  • Delivered a scalable real-time 3D solution

The result was smooth real-time interaction and a property accessible to anyone with a browser.
bodies.role:
I ran this as Technical Project Manager, between the client and the delivery team.

  • Managed client communication and requirement definition
  • Documented the functional requirements
  • Planned and managed the Agile sprints
  • Coordinated tasks for the development and QA teams
  • Led the feature delivery process

items.title: ePOS System
items.problem: A web-based point-of-sale system in Japan handles high-value financial transactions for hundreds of daily users, where any instability is a direct business risk.
items.solution: Feature development and production hardening of the SPA inside a distributed enterprise platform.
items.impact: Reduced production issues, with improved reliability and user trust in a critical financial system.
items.role: Front-end engineer on the team: features, requirement analysis, production investigation and mentoring.

bodies.business:
A web-based ePOS system used in Japan for managing high-value financial transactions. It forms part of a distributed enterprise platform and is used daily by hundreds of people.

  • High reliability and accuracy required of every transaction
  • Instability in a financial system costs trust, not just time
  • Production issues needed diagnosis without disrupting daily operations
bodies.solution:
Sustained feature delivery alongside production hardening, keeping a critical system stable while it continued to change.

  • Performed root cause analysis on production issues
  • Collaborated closely with the QA and backend teams
  • Supported continuous delivery without compromising quality

The outcome was fewer production issues and improved reliability for financial operations.
bodies.role:
I worked as a front-end engineer and team contributor on the single-page application.

  • Developed new features for the SPA
  • Performed requirement analysis and approach design
  • Investigated and fixed production issues
  • Mentored junior team members

items.title: Data Visualization Web Application
items.problem: Large volumes of data had to be made explorable on both desktop and mobile, without the interface slowing to a crawl.
items.solution: A structured web application for filtering and analysing data, sitting inside a larger cloud-based architecture.
items.impact: Improved data accessibility and usability, enabling faster decision-making from the same data.
items.role: Front-end developer across teams: UI components, API integration and test specifications.

bodies.business:
A large volume of data existed but was not usable. It needed to be presented in a structured, readable way, on desktop and on mobile, as part of a larger cloud-based architecture.

  • Data too voluminous to browse without filtering
  • Both desktop and mobile interfaces to support
  • Rendering large datasets efficiently was the core constraint
bodies.solution:
A web application that presents data in a structured, user-friendly way and lets people filter and analyse it directly.

  • Optimized data fetching and rendering for large datasets
  • Built reusable UI components across the interface
  • Ensured quality through structured unit and integration testing

The result was a smooth, efficient experience and faster decision-making from data that had been sitting unread.
bodies.role:
I worked as a front-end developer contributing across teams.

  • Developed the UI components and layouts
  • Integrated APIs and handled data processing
  • Created a mock UI for client validation
  • Prepared the test specifications and reports
  • Performed unit and integration testing
